entry.title: Automate CSV to Parquet with Buckets, Webhooks & Jobs

media:group.media:title: Automate CSV to Parquet with Buckets, Webhooks & Jobs
media:group.media:description:
Files keep landing in your Hugging Face Storage Bucket. Here is how to process each one automatically, without downloading anything.
In this live-coding video we set up a webhook on a bucket that triggers a Hugging Face Job whenever a new file arrives. The Job runs the `optimize-parquet.py` uv script, converts the new CSV to optimized Parquet, and writes it to a second bucket. We upload a 10,000-row slice of the NYC taxi dataset, and the triggered Job finishes in about 8 seconds. For data engineers already using Buckets who want to automate what happens next.
Topics covered: - Hugging Face Storage Buckets with the hf CLI - Running a uv script as a Hugging Face Job - Webhooks that trigger Jobs on bucket changes - Converting CSV to Parquet automatically - Checking Job status, logs and output
Resources: - Webhooks guide (bucket to Jobs): https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/webhooks-guide-bucket-jobs - optimize-parquet.py script: https://huggingface.co/datasets/uv-scripts/data-processing/raw/main/optimize-parquet.py - My notes and demo code: https://github.com/prpatel/simple-buckets-demo - Hands-on with Buckets (article): https://huggingface.co/blog/prpatel/hands-on-with-buckets

entry.title: Pi Durable: AI agents that survive crashes

media:group.media:title: Pi Durable: AI agents that survive crashes
media:group.media:description:
Your agent sent 4 of 5 emails… then crashed. A regular coding agent leaves you with a half-finished tool call and a "continue" prayer. Pi Durable checkpoints every task and tool call (SQLite / JSONL), so when the process restarts, the agent resumes where it left off.
It's not a CLI. It's a TypeScript library for building always-on agents, even fully local with Qwen3.5-0.8B on llama.cpp.
▶ Full tutorial: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ti3vVYwzW4A 💻 Demo code: https://github.com/alejandro-ao/pi-durable-demo

entry.title: Pi Durable EXPLAINED: Build Always-On Agents with Local Models

media:group.media:title: Pi Durable EXPLAINED: Build Always-On Agents with Local Models
media:group.media:description:
Pi Durable is a building block for always-on agent applications, not a new coding-agent CLI. Learn how checkpoints, conversations, and storage support recovery after interruptions, where Durable fits in the Pi ecosystem, and the six steps to initialize a harness. Then follow a local llama.cpp demo with Qwen3.5-0.8B, including a second script that resumes interrupted work from SQLite. The APIs are experimental and may change; tool replay safety and restarting the host process remain important application responsibilities.

entry.title: HF Buckets: Upload Only What Changed with Xet

media:group.media:title: HF Buckets: Upload Only What Changed with Xet
media:group.media:description:
If you work with large datasets, you're probably re-uploading the same bytes every time the data changes.
In this video I upload a 191 MB NYC taxi CSV to a Hugging Face Bucket, append 100 rows, and upload it again: Xet, Hugging Face's storage layer, sends only the new pieces. Then I convert the data to Parquet, prepend 100 rows, and sync again: with PyArrow's use_content_defined_chunking=True, only 8.6 MB of the 52.9 MB file goes over the wire. For data and ML engineers who push datasets to the Hub and keep them up to date.
Topics covered: - How Xet uploads only the pieces that changed - Hugging Face Buckets with the hf CLI (create, cp, sync) - Content-defined Parquet blocks with PyArrow 21+ - Upload savings: ~90 MB vs ~6 MB on a 100 MB file - Production gotchas: S3 tools, versioning, sorting, writer settings
Resources: - Full walkthrough (commands, code, dataset): https://huggingface.co/blog/prpatel/hands-on-with-buckets - Hugging Face forum: https://discuss.huggingface.co/
Chapters: 0:00 Stop wasting bandwidth 0:15 What you'll see 0:39 Demo: CSV and Parquet uploads to a Bucket 9:11 Xet, in three steps 10:10 The one-line fix 10:47 How much Xet saves 11:13 Before you ship it 12:27 Join the discussion
